Review of run r-20260921T065359899293-fleet-throttling-baseline (node fleet-throttling-baseline), plan imas-ambix:slurm-hosted-agent-fleet section 7 throttling baseline. Reviewed commits 0805cb74, 3a59eccf and cff4e0d5 against base a6800ced. Artifact under review: imas_ambix/agent/throttling.py, tests/agent/test_throttling.py, the anchored evidence section in docs/evidence/archive/slurm-hosted-agent-fleet-landed.html and the landing record in docs/plans/slurm-hosted-agent-fleet.html. This review re-ran two things and no more: the named unit gate (22 passed, exit 0) and the whole-tree lint gate (exit 0).

FOUR QUESTIONS, ANSWERED WITH EVIDENCE.

Q(a) Is the negative control the run actually executed the one its dispatch declared? VERDICT: NO. The stored run record (live pointer r-20260921T065359899293-fleet-throttling-baseline.json, field node.negative_control) declares: "in the throttled-share computation, replace the quota divisor taken from cpu.max with the constant 1.0 so the share is computed against one core rather than against the configured quota; the test asserting the share against a known fixture must be observed to fail, and the failing pytest output recorded". The negative-control log's own first line reads: "DECLARED MUTATION: in imas_ambix/agent/throttling.py, throttled_share returns 0.0 instead of None for a control group with no ceiling (cpu.max quota field is the literal `max`), so an unquota-ed group reports a zero share rather than an undefined one." These are different mutations in different branches of different functions: one divides by the wrong number in the quota-ed path, the other returns zero instead of an undefined sentinel in the unquota-ed path, and each reddens a different set of tests. Evidence that the declared text never reached the worker at all: grep -c "quota divisor" returns 0 in the run's own prompt.txt and 0 in its stream.jsonl, so the log's "DECLARED MUTATION:" label cannot be a repeat of the declaration it names, and a dispatch path that fails to transmit the declared control is a second defect beside the run's. Independently reproduced in memory against the shipped source, without editing files: the declared mutation fails four shipped test bodies (cumulative share, permitted thread time, share-passes-one, interval share), so it was discriminating and runnable yet was never applied; the applied mutation fails exactly the two tests the log names, so the log's account of what it did is truthful and only its label is false.

Q(b) Can the cumulative throttled share the run reports be re-derived from the raw counters it also reports? VERDICT: YES. Arithmetic: nr_periods 37,199,459 multiplied by the quota 400,000 usec gives 14,879,783,600,000 usec of permitted thread-time (the period cancels against the quota); 5,008,386,657,643 usec of throttled thread-time divided by 14,879,783,600,000 usec gives 0.3365900198738777, which rounds to the reported 0.3366. The permitted_usec the run's table records is exactly 14,879,783,600,000, so its own table is internally consistent, and recomputing with the module's own permitted_thread_usec and throttled_share over the recorded counters returns the same two values; the single-window live reading in logs/live_sample.log (0.33649944721997904) is the same computation on a second live read.

Q(c) Does the sampler return an undefined rather than a zero share for a control group with no ceiling, and could any caller misread that as zero? VERDICT: YES it returns undefined, WITH ONE RESIDUAL TRAP. imas_ambix/agent/throttling.py:150-153 returns None whenever the permitted total is absent, and permitted_thread_usec at :125-135 returns None when cpu.max's quota field is the literal max; _counters_payload at :190-198 serialises that as JSON null rather than 0, and tests/agent/test_throttling.py:115 pins is None for the unquota-ed case with :176 pinning the interval case. No shipped caller exists: grep finds no import of the module outside its own test, so nothing in the tree misreads it today (the run's own follow-on 2 says the sampler is not yet wired to any monitor). The trap is for the first caller: a consumer writing share or 0.0 (or any truthiness test) converts an unbounded group's null into 0.0, which is precisely the reading the module docstring at :8-13 exists to prevent, and the property that discriminates the two cases, CpuMax.can_throttle at :44-47, is itself read by no shipped code. A smaller collapse sits beside it: two distinct undefined causes (no ceiling; zero periods accounted) return the same None, so a consumer cannot tell "unbounded" from "no window yet" without reading cpu_max itself. Neither is a defect against the fence, which asks exactly for undefined-not-zero and gets it.

Q(d) Was the negative control exercised against the same set of checks that finally shipped? VERDICT: NO. The control's log records "collected 21 items ...  2 failed, 19 passed" with NEGCTL_EXIT=1, and its file mtimes sit at 08:58:50 through 09:01:28; 21 collected is the revision the run had at commit 0805cb74, which carries 16 test functions (21 collected once the parametrised case expands), whereas the final gate log logs/test_exact_command.log records 22 passed and HEAD's tests/agent/test_throttling.py holds 17 functions collecting 22. The 22nd collected case is tests/agent/test_throttling.py:122 test_share_passes_one_when_more_tasks_stall_than_the_ceiling_admits, added by commit 3a59eccf at 09:01:28 -- the same commit that added the docstring paragraph stating the share can pass one; git show --stat confirms 3a59eccf touches only imas_ambix/agent/throttling.py (+6) and tests/agent/test_throttling.py (+10). So the control ran before the last behaviour landed, that behaviour was never exercised against any mutation, and the control's own restored-tree re-run (21 passed) reflects the smaller suite rather than the shipped one.

VERDICT goal: the node's goal is a committed cgroup v2 CPU-throttling sampler for the account user slice together with the baseline share it measures on the login node (prompt.txt:25); imas_ambix/agent/throttling.py:138 computes the cumulative and the interval share from passed-in text, :116 reads one control group's two files, and :214 carries the module's own main(), so the sampler is committed and the live 0.3366 baseline is recorded.

VERDICT done_when: the quantitative fence is the seven-item evidence list at prompt.txt:39-58; items 1, 2, 4, 5, 6 and 7 are recorded with receipts and re-checked here (22 passed, exit 0; whole-tree ruff exit 0; the counters reproduce as in Q(b)), but item 3 is satisfied only in mechanism -- the mutation applied is not the one the run record declares (Q(a)) -- and its scope is one revision short of the shipped suite (Q(d)).

VERDICT write_paths: the declared paths are imas_ambix/agent/throttling.py, tests/agent/test_throttling.py, docs/plans/slurm-hosted-agent-fleet.html and docs/evidence/archive/slurm-hosted-agent-fleet-landed.html; every file in the three commits is inside them and imas_ambix/agent/cli.py, which another node owns, is untouched.

VERDICT manifest: read; it records the 22-passed gate, the live sample and series logs, the negative-control log and the raw counters it derived them from, and it claims all seven fence items met -- which is not accurate for item 3, whose control was a different mutation than the one the run record declares, and for the declared mutation's absence from the worker's input no manifest entry can speak.
